title: S switches timeline snapping off and on
goal: Clips snap to the playhead, cuts and each other while you drag them, which is right most of the time, but there is no way to turn it off for a fine placement. Premiere and Final Cut both switch snapping with S and show a magnet that says whether it is on.
notes: Found by measure-the-video-editor-against-premiere-and-fi (2026-09-24); gap report docs/design/video-vs-premiere.md. Reproduced: s with the timeline focused is taken by nobody (five-minute walk step 21). No toggle exists in Sources (grep 'snapping' in the timeline files only finds the key snap reach). Holding a modifier to suspend snapping while dragging is fine as well, if the walk shows it.
acceptance: S with the timeline focused switches snapping, and a magnet button in the timeline bar shows and switches the same state
With snapping off, a clip dragged near the playhead lands where it is let go
A walk switches snapping off, drags a clip to 0.1 s from the playhead and it lands there
Works at Next defaults with no switch turned on, and an audit written under queue/audits/ gives the try steps and a real picture
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Review before building: Premiere and Final Cut both put snapping on S with a magnet that shows its state; the mock's timeline bar (video.html .tlbar) draws no snapping control, so the magnet is an addition past the floor, placed after Select and Blade behind a divider so it reads as a switch, not a third tool. S is free on a focused timeline (on the canvas it stays the tool key). Snapping is a mode, not a verb, so it goes in the menu bar (Video > Snap in Timeline, Premiere's name) rather than a right-click menu. The switch covers every snap the timeline makes: clip bars (move, trim, seam), files dropped on the timeline, and the playhead catching on keys. The old recording window's trim strip is left alone.

Built: TimelineKeys s -> toggleSnapping; ClipBarDrag.snapping(withinMS:) so S mid-drag re-lands from the hand; EditorState.isTimelineSnapping (per window, on by default) gating clipSnapMS, the drop reach and keySnapReachMS; magnet button (drawn MagnetGlyph, SF Symbols has none) in TimelineDock's bar; Video menu toggle; walk claim expectTimeline.snapping and action clipSlideShortOfPlayhead. Tests: Scripts/test.sh 9652 passed. Walk snapping-switches-with-s-walk: at Next defaults, no flags, 5-minute hold so the catch reach is 2 s; snapping on a slide 0.1 s short lands on the playhead (75.00), S off it lands 74.90, magnet click turns it back on, S mid-drag lets go of a catch (74.97). Neighbours a-clip-shows-where-it-will-land, second-clip-on-the-timeline, library-clip-onto-a-track, ripple-trim-to-playhead, timeline-keys-on-open all ok.

left rough (not filed, below the bar): snapping is per window and resets to on for each new window, where Premiere remembers the last setting; chosen so an off left over from yesterday does not read as snapping being broken, and put to the user as an evaluate question in the audit rather than filed. The walk slides the clip through the harness (the same drag model the pointer drives), not a real pointer; the S press and the magnet click are real.

S on a focused timeline, a magnet button in the timeline's bar and Video > Snap in Timeline switch timeline snapping (clip moves, trims, file drops, playhead on keys); S mid-drag takes effect at once.
